America’s national debt has been rising for decades, but when does it actually become a problem ordinary people can feel?

This video explores the moment when government debt stops being an abstract number and starts competing directly with the things taxpayers expect their money to fund.
In 2024, U.S. net interest costs reached roughly $882 billion, surpassing national defense spending. As older low-interest debt is refinanced at higher rates, that bill continues to grow, leaving less room for everything else. The consequences could spread far beyond Washington. Higher borrowing costs put pressure on businesses, housing, investment, and wages. Social Security faces its own funding challenges, while companies dependent on cheap debt become increasingly vulnerable as interest rates rise. But the most important question is what happens if the government keeps borrowing instead of closing the gap.
title: The Day The National Debt Actually Becomes a Problem
